newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium alloy price seen higher by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium alloy price seen higher by year-end.

text.p: Aluminium alloy prices are seen remaining under pressure in the immediate short-term before strengthening towards the end of the year, London Metal Exchange (LME) trader Rudolf Wolff and Co said.
In a special report on the aluminium alloy market Wolff said that after the seasonally slow summer months prices should pick up and return to the year highs of $1,500.

"The prospects for growth in the secondary aluminium market are improving in the medium to longer term, which is likely to have a positive effect on the LME contract," Wolff analyst Martin Squires said.
The main growth area will be increased demand from the transport sector which accounts for over 65 percent of Western world consumption annually..

"The principal expansion in the transport sector is expected to come from Sout East Asia, whose economies are growing at around eight percent a year, and other developing countries, such as China," Wolff said.
The main supportive factor for a stronger alloy price is the likely sustained recovery in the U.S and Japanese economies, which should impact on ailing European markets.
Wolff noted that increased aluminium usage in automoble production will also feed through to boost alloy demand.
Contained aluminium in cars is seen rising from the current level of 252 lbs to 347 lbs by the year 2000 - a 37 percent increase.
"As a result of this increased demand the alloy market is also likely to see a considerable increase in consumption over the next few years," the report said.
Meanwhile, the discount of alloy prices to primary aluminium is expected to narrow. Alloy may even move to a premium as happened in 1994.
"This arises because the supply of alloy is limited during certain stages of the business cycle," it added.
